title: Islet Culture and Preparation for Cold Shipping
author: Integrated Islet Distribution Program
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfsfjnbn
materials: Receipt of Supplies: The majority of supplies should be stored in appropriate dry, temperature-controlled environments (room temperature 16°-28°C). The Prodo Labs PIM(R) should be stored, in the dark, between 2 °C and 8 °C upon receipt but is stable at room temperature. The Gemini AB serum and the PIM(G) vials should be stored at -5 °C to -20 °C in the dark. The Ciprofloxacin should be stored as indicated by manufacturer (Corning at room temperature OR MP Biomedicals at 4°C). Aliquots of Ciprofloxin can be prepared prior to the isolation. Prepare the Ciprofloxacin according to the directions in the table. Filter sterilized suspension aliquots should be stored at -5 °C to -20 °C . Record Ciprofloxacin preparation on Attachment 1: Solutions Preparation Sheet , of this SOP. Attachment 1-Solutions preparation Sheets.pdf

Laboratory Supplies: The following supplies are necessary for the preparation of flasks for human islet culture prior to distribution. Islet preparation and distribution Wide mouth pipettes and pipettor Culture flasks- T-175 non-coated flasks Sampling wide-bore pipette tip and pipettor (Gilson or Drummond) 37°C CO 2 Incubator Conical tubes, 250 ml, sterile Routine lab supplies for transferring, media changing and counting islets.

steps.title: Prepare PIM(R) Complete Media
steps.instruction: In a sterile 500 mL bottle add 5 mL PIM(G), 25 mL human AB serum (5 % v/v), and 0.5 mL sterile ciprofloxacin aliquot; mix to obtain PIM(R) complete. If total islet mass exceeds 250,000 IEQ prepare a second bottle. Any reused bottle must be filter‑sterilized at the end of the previous use. Record preparation on Attachment 1. Media expires 30 days after full supplementation.

steps.title: Resuspend Purified Islets
steps.instruction: Transfer pooled islets with >70 % purity into 200 mL PIM(R) within a 250 mL conical and mix by pouring between two conicals or inverting at least three times.

steps.title: Sample and Stain Islets
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑bore pipette tip, take two 100–200 µL samples from the well‑mixed suspension (one per technician). Add 3 drops (≈30 µL) DTZ solution, stain 1–2 min at room temperature, cover the counting dish bottom with DPBS to ~½ the dish height, and count islets under the microscope as described in the DTZ SOP. Keep the conical on its side in the hood during counting. Record counts on Attachment 2.

steps.title: Calculate IEQ Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the average IEQ count, then compute total IEQs and IEQ per mL (e.g., 250,000 IEQ ÷ 200 mL = 1,250 IEQ/mL).

steps.title: Determine Flask Volume per 20k IEQ
steps.instruction: Divide 20,000 IEQ by the IEQ/mL value to obtain the suspension volume required per T‑175 flask (e.g., 20,000 ÷ 1,250 = 16 mL/flask).

steps.title: Calculate Number of Flasks
steps.instruction: Divide total IEQs by 20,000 IEQ to get required flasks, round up to the next whole number, then recalculate suspension volume per flask (e.g., 12.5 → 13 flasks; 200 mL ÷ 13 = 15.4 mL/flask). Compute fresh PIM(R) needed to pre‑wet each flask (e.g., 40 mL total – 15.4 mL suspension = 24.6 mL fresh media).

steps.title: Pre‑wet and Label Flasks
steps.instruction: Aseptically bring the required number of non‑coated T‑175 flasks into the hood, label per center protocol, pre‑wet all but one flask with the calculated fresh PIM(R) volume; pre‑wet the final flask with 6 mL less than the calculated amount and mark it as the final flask.

steps.title: Distribute Islet Suspension
steps.instruction: Lay flasks flat on the hood surface, ensuring media covers the entire surface without wetting the neck or cap. Using a 25 mL pipette, deliver ~20,000 IEQ (≈15.4 mL suspension) to each flask, mixing the suspension between flasks for even distribution.

steps.title: Rinse Conical and Adjust Volume
steps.instruction: After loading the final flask, rinse the conical with 3 mL extra media; repeat as needed so each flask contains a total volume of 40 mL.

steps.title: Incubate Flasks
steps.instruction: Place all flasks upright in a 37 °C ± 0.5 °C, 5 % ± 0.5 % CO₂ incubator and culture for at least 48 hours (see Attachment 4 for possible exceptions).

steps.title: First Half‑Media Change (12‑18 h)
steps.instruction: Between 12 and 18 hours after culture start, perform a 50 % media change on all flasks following the Half Media Change Procedure (steps 5‑14 of that SOP).

steps.title: Adjust for Purity‑Based Flasks
steps.instruction: If islet purity is less than 100 %, recalculate the number of flasks using total IEQs ÷ (20,000 IEQ × purity). Example: 50 % purity, 50,000 IEQ → 5 flasks. Re‑determine all volumes accordingly. Note: Islets <50 % purity are not eligible for reimbursement.

steps.title: Day‑1 Half‑Media Change
steps.instruction: Perform a half‑culture‑volume media change 18‑24 hours after isolation (Day 1). If shipment will occur after Day 5, perform a second half‑media change.

steps.title: Warm Fresh Media
steps.instruction: Remove the required volume of PIM(R) from the refrigerator at least 1 hour before the media change, allow it to reach room temperature, and place it aseptically in the laminar flow hood.

steps.title: Remove and Rock Flasks
steps.instruction: Transport flasks vertically (cap up) from the incubator to the hood, rock them gently back‑and‑forth while horizontal to detach loosely attached islets (avoid media entering caps), then return them upright and loosen the caps.

steps.title: Arrange Flasks for Settling
steps.instruction: For each set of 10 flasks, place a 250 mL conical rack supporting a 50 mL conical rack; position five flasks per row, tilting each toward the longer edge so islets settle in the lower corner. Start a 45‑minute timer and record the start time in the batch record.

steps.title: Allow Islets to Settle
steps.instruction: Leave the flasks in the angled position for 45 minutes to allow islets to settle at the bottom corner surface.

steps.title: Check Islet Size in Media
steps.instruction: Withdraw 1 mL from the middle of the media in a flask, place it in a Petri dish, and examine under a microscope. If islets are <50 µm, proceed; if larger islets are present, allow additional settling time and repeat.

steps.title: Aspirate Used Media
steps.instruction: While maintaining the flask angle, aspirate 50 % of the media (≈20 mL) from the surface, equidistant from the sides, without disturbing the settled islets.

steps.title: Collect Aspirated Media
steps.instruction: Transfer the aspirated media into a sterile empty container (allows recovery of viable islets). Repeat for all flasks.

steps.title: Add Fresh Media
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 mL fresh PIM(R) into each flask and tighten the caps.

steps.title: Finalize Media Change
steps.instruction: Inspect the collected aspirate for any islets >50 µm; transfer such islets to a flask. Verify all caps are tight and return flasks to the incubator set to 37 °C ± 0.5 °C.

steps.title: Filter Sterilize Remaining Media
steps.instruction: Using a 0.2 µm filter, sterilize any remaining fresh PIM(R) complete media; note that supplemented media expires 30 days after preparation.

steps.title: Supplies Provided by IIDP
steps.instruction: The IIDP supplies Human AB Serum (ABS) HI, PIM(G)®, PIM(R)®, and Ciprofloxacin Hydrochloride for use in this protocol.
